# Fast Twitter (X) User Scraper API | Extract Profiles, Followers

The Apify actor [`apidojo/twitter-user-scraper`](https://apify.com/apidojo/twitter-user-scraper) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its default build **0.0.1212** (module version **0.1.0**). Runs use whatever build the actor has as default when they start, so they keep working as Apify retires old builds; the input types below are refreshed weekly and can lag an actor that changed its input since.

Introducing Twitter (X) User Scraper, the ultimate solution for direct user extraction from Twitter (X). It offers blazing speed and comprehensiveness, delivering lightning-fast user extraction features.

## Pricing

Pay per event — Dataset Item $0.0004, Profile About Query $0.0002, Retweeters Query $0.016, Following Query $0.016, Follower Query $0.016, Profile URL Query $0.004, Keyword Search $0.008 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/apidojo/twitter-user-scraper) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/apidojo-twitter-user-scraper@0.1.0#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs: {}
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
